name: sol_hmt_1
description: Merkle root update front-runnable, letting attackers exploit stale/new proof window before impact
question: The source file in `source` defines a function that sets or updates a Merkle root used for proof verification (e.g., claims, whitelist, airdrop) such that between the transaction submitting the new root and its confirmation, users or attackers can observe the pending root/proof and front-run the update to claim, exploit stale eligibility, or extract value based on knowledge of the new or old root, with no safeguard such as a commit-reveal scheme, delay plus cutoff, or invalidation of in-flight claims tied to the old root. This excludes Merkle root updates that are restricted to a trusted admin only for legitimate configuration changes where front-running has no exploitable financial impact, or designs that already implement a timelock, pending-root reveal, or root-versioning mechanism preventing race exploitation.
criteria: setMerkleRoot() lets anyone claim() immediately after root update with no delay, allowing attacker to front-run using the new root before eligible users act
updateRoot() changes root directly in same tx as reward distribution, letting an attacker see the mempool tx and submit a competing claim first to drain funds
claim() checks proof against a root that can be changed by admin in the same block without invalidating pending claims, enabling double-claim across old and new root
Merkle-based airdrop allows claiming with old root proof even after root update tx is pending, letting user front-run the update to claim twice
